 Gold, silver rates today, November 16: Gold ₹780 below its Nov 9 peak; silver down 9.5% from Nov 5 high
 By Upstox News Desk 4 min read | Updated on November 16, 2026, 14:11 IST
 Preferred news source Select Upstox as your Preferred news source SUMMARY
 Gold and silver fell on Monday as trading resumed, with 24 karat at ₹13,680 a gram and silver at ₹190 a gram, leaving gold ₹208 below its November 1 level and silver 5.00% lower than at the start of the month.
 Gold and silver prices have declined in November till now. | Image: Shutterstock
 Gold prices resumed their decline on Monday, November 16, with 24 karat price at ₹13,680 per gram and 22 karat at ₹12,540, according to GoodReturns data. Silver fell ₹5 to ₹190 a gram, or ₹1,90,000 a kilogram. It is the lowest rate for both metals in the last 10 days.

 Data shows that the 10 grams of 24 karat now costs ₹1,36,800, 22 karat ₹1,25,400 and 18 karat ₹1,02,600. In Delhi, the price was a little higher ob Monday with 24 karat gold at ₹13,695 a gram, with 22 karat at ₹12,555 and 18 karat at ₹10,275, while Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Kerala were all at around ₹13,680 a gram.

 Both metals have now given up most of the gains added during the festive fortnight. As of today, Gold is ₹208 a gram, or 1.50%, below its November 1 level of ₹13,888, ₹677 below its Diwali rate of ₹14,357, and ₹780 below the ₹14,460 it touched on November 9. Silver has done worse. At ₹190 a gram, it is 5% below November 1 and 9.52% below the ₹210 a gram, or ₹2,10,000 a kilogram, it commanded on November 5.

 Silver rates in India on three dates in November 2026 
 Monday's fall matters for a different reason than the earlier ones. After Diwali, the metal slid for four sessions, steadied on Friday and Saturday, and has now given way again as the market reopened, which suggests the weakness is not simply the unwinding of a single week of festival purchases. The pattern is common to both metals. Prices rose into Dhanteras and Diwali, with gold gaining ₹714 a gram over four sessions to November 5 and silver touching its November high of ₹2,10,000 a kilogram the same day. They have been retreating since as festival demand ended and holders who had bought into the rally sold.
 Silver's fall is steeper in percentage terms because the metal moves more sharply than gold in both directions and is more exposed to industrial demand.
 For households buying for the wedding season, which begins later this month, the entry price has improved for the third week running.
 Please note that gold and silver rates published online are indicative and they may vary between jewellers and cities.
 Whether the slide continues depends on the rupee and on the dollar price of the metal overseas, neither of which has offered support this month. With the wedding season spread over weeks rather than concentrated on a single day, the market has no obvious trigger in either direction before the next festival demand cycle.
